string-array.name: municipalities_array
string-array.item: Beijing, the capital of China and its second-largest city, has served as the political, cultural and educational centre of the nation for more than eight centuries. It is famed for imperial landmarks including the Forbidden City, the Temple of Heaven, Tiananmen Square and sections of the Great Wall at Badaling and Mutianyu. As host of the 2008 Summer and 2022 Winter Olympic Games, Beijing combines dynasties-old heritage with a modern global hub for technology, finance and diplomacy. Its metropolitan area is home to over 21 million residents and is connected by one of the longest subway systems in the world and the vast Beijing Daxing International Airport.

Shanghai, the largest city in China and a global financial and trade centre, sits on the estuary of the Yangtze River on the central coast of the country. It is famous for the colonial waterfront skyline of the Bund and the futuristic towers of Lujiazui, including the 632-metre Shanghai Tower. Beyond the skyscrapers, visitors can explore the tree-lined lanes of the former French Concession, the classical Yu Garden and a celebrated food scene. The Port of Shanghai is the busiest container harbour in the world, anchoring a metropolitan region of roughly 24 million people.

Chongqing is one of the four direct-administered municipalities of China, located in the southwest where the Yangtze and Jialing rivers meet among steep, mist-shrouded hills. Known for its extraordinary topography, monorails that pass straight through residential buildings, and fiery Sichuan hotpot, it is a major industrial, manufacturing and river-shipping hub. The historic Ciqikou town, the stilted houses of Hongyadong and the nearby Three Gorges draw millions of visitors each year. Its vast municipal territory contains more than 32 million residents, making it one of the most populous cities in China.

Tianjin is a direct-administered municipality on the Bohai Sea coast in northern China, roughly thirty kilometres southeast of Beijing. Originating as a Ming-dynasty military garrison, it later became a major treaty port, leaving a distinctive legacy of colonial architecture along the Five Great Avenues. Today Tianjin is a busy port, industrial and educational centre, known for the Tianjin Eye ferris wheel spanning the Hai River and the modern skyline of Binhai New Area. Its convenient rail link to Beijing has helped it grow into a metropolis of around 13 million residents.
